about: DRAFT element-to-affordance relevance claims for a composed TA02 Secure Possession activity (K6). Every claim is PROPOSED, for Christian's review, and none is approved. Each claim names the element (by the knowledge item that establishes it), the affordance it is claimed to serve, the relation, the knowledge rows that support it, and whether the support is authored knowledge or our reading. Paths are relative to the worktree C:/challenge-point/.claude/worktrees/serene-dewdney-c78e18 (HEAD f5d6d24). Nothing in the repo was changed. The 'consequence' sentences are OUR WORDING in plain language and are not coach-facing.

supportLevels.AUTHORED_RELATIONSHIP: An authored row itself relates the element's source to GP-015 or to the affordance (the join from element to that row is the contract's own basisEvidence). Ours is only the reading that the relation is a relevance relation.
supportLevels.AUTHORED_TEXT_CORRESPONDENCE: Authored text on the element (an approved condition) states the same relation the Game Problem's definition commits to; the claim joining them is ours.
supportLevels.AUTHORED_PREMISES_OUR_JOIN: Every premise is authored (the element's item and its basis, the affordance's rating and name), but no authored row joins them; the join is ours.
supportLevels.OUR_READING: At least one premise of the claim is our reading of play or of coaching meaning; nothing authored states it.

relations.MAKES_AVAILABLE: The element creates the opportunity at all (without it the affordance could not occur in this game).
relations.SHAPES: The element changes when, where or how often the opportunity occurs, or what losing it costs.
relations.PROTECTS: The element prevents a degenerate solution that would remove the opportunity or make it terminal.
relations.PRESERVES_INFORMATION: The element keeps the information the opportunity depends on available to players.

a01RationaleShape.type: back/src/system/test-library/learning-goal-authorizations.ts:355 'rationale: { feature: string; words: CitedWords[]; statements: string[] }[]'
a01RationaleShape.validation: learning-goal-authorizations.ts:407-411: each entry must name the feature and quote only his reasons, each cited; statements must be non-empty strings
a01RationaleShape.consumer: back/src/system/rendering/review-evidence.ts:1212-1223 (admin review evidence only; featureBasis 'OURS' at :359 and :1217; statements resolved only against rpcLibrary.properties(record.contextId)), summarized at :1290

fields.feature: Free-text label of an activity feature, OURS (for example 'The building team has more players than the pressing team (the starting configuration)').
fields.words: HIS reasons, verbatim, each with citedAs (for example his 17 Oct D6 words on numerical advantage).
fields.statements: RPC property ids of the record's own context only (for example RPC-PROP-017, RPC-PROP-132, RPC-PROP-010); ids outside that context resolve to null text.

whatItCannotDoForComposition: It is authored per activity version: the features are the realization's features and the reasons are his words given about that version. A composed activity has no such words, and the validator refuses an entry without them.
The feature is prose. It joins to no element, contract item or ElementProvenance, so nothing can check that the feature exists in the game.
It names no affordance and no Game Problem dimension, so it cannot show which of GP-015's Essential affordances an element serves, or that all are served.
Its statements may cite only the context's properties: not GF2 items, GAK rows, ATM rows, or constraint records.
It has no status (PROPOSED / APPROVED) and no separation of authored support from our reading beyond the single featureBasis 'OURS'.

proposedGeneralShape.status: PROPOSED, ours, for his review (D8 decides vocabulary and whether the check is a gate or evidence)
proposedGeneralShape.principle: A relevance claim attaches to KNOWLEDGE, not to an activity version: (knowledge item that establishes an element) x (affordance in a vocabulary he approves) x (relation). It is written once and applies to every composition that contains the item, for every Game Problem whose profile rates that affordance. A goal-specific reading (item x Learning Goal row) is a separate, optional layer, flagged as such. Engine join (E7): ElementProvenance -> origin item -> claims on that item -> affordance -> GP profile rating.

claim.establishedBy: [{ contractId, itemId }] (the origin items; resolvable through ElementProvenance)
claim.appliesWhen: optional: other items that must also be present (for example EL-05 + EL-04)
claim.consequence: plain-language environmental consequence (OURS until he approves wording; if coach-facing, a concise Coach Details consequence explanation, which his 24 October reply permits when grounded in authorized knowledge, christian-2026-10-24.txt:40, :50)
claim.support: [{ kind: AUTHORED | OWNER_RULING | AUTHORED_RELATIONSHIP | LIBRARY_TEXT_DRAFT_MODULE | HIS_WORDS_GENERAL_PRINCIPLE | HIS_WORDS_OTHER_GOAL | ASSUMED_ITEM, ref (row id), path (file:line or JSON path), quote (verbatim) }]
claim.ruling: his words and citation, only when status is APPROVED (never filled by us)

goalReading.rows: [Learning Goal / Practice Situation row text, verbatim]
goalReading.supportLevel: as above (almost always OUR_READING until he rules)

checks: Every non-inherited element in a composed game has at least one claim to an affordance its Game Problem rates Essential (reported, not a gate, unless he rules otherwise).
Every Essential affordance of the Game Problem is served by at least one non-INERT claim.
The primary scoring element carries a claim, and RPC-VAL-012 is reported against it.
A claim whose establishing item reaches no element in the realized game is reported INERT (the silent-loss lesson: a claim is proved only by a consumer).
proposedGeneralShape.difference from A01's rationale: A01's rationale is his reasons for one authored version; this shape is our proposed claims about reusable knowledge, approved claim by claim. The two can coexist: an approved claim may carry his words in 'ruling', which is what A01's 'words' are.
